claim: MAF1 is a key repressor of RNA polymerase (pol) III-mediated transcription.
source: MAF1, a key repressor of RNA polymerase (pol) III-mediated transcription, has been shown to promote mesoderm formation in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Graczyk et al., 2015; Johnson et al., 2007).

claim: MAF1 has been shown to promote mesoderm formation in vitro.
source: MAF1, a key repressor of RNA polymerase (pol) III-mediated transcription, has been shown to promote mesoderm formation in vitro.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by citation to Chen et al., 2018 in the introduction.

claim: Global deletion of MAF1 (Maf1-/- mice) produced a high bone mass phenotype.
source: Global deletion of MAF1 (Maf1-/- mice) produced a high bone mass phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by µCT data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Osteoblasts isolated from Maf1-/- mice showed reduced osteoblastogenesis ex vivo.
source: However, osteoblasts isolated from Maf1-/- mice showed reduced osteoblastogenesis ex vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mice overexpressing MAF1 in cells from the mesenchymal lineage (Prx1-Cre;LSL-MAF1 mice) showed increased bone mass.
source: Therefore, we determined the phenotype of mice overexpressing MAF1 in cells from the mesenchymal lineage (Prx1-Cre;LSL-MAF1 mice). These mice showed increased bone mass.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by µCT data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cells from Prx1-Cre;LSL-MAF1 mice showed enhanced osteoblastogenesis ex vivo.
source: Ex vivo, cells from these mice showed enhanced osteoblastogenesis concordant with their high bone mass phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by alizarin red staining data in Figure 1F.

claim: The high bone mass phenotype in Maf1-/- mice is likely due to confounding effects from the global absence of MAF1.
source: Thus, the high bone mass phenotype in Maf1-/- mice is likely due to confounding effects from the global absence of MAF1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the contrasting ex vivo and in vivo phenotypes observed in Maf1-/- mice compared to tissue-specific overexpression.

claim: MAF1 overexpression promoted osteoblast differentiation of ST2 cells.
source: MAF1 overexpression promoted osteoblast differentiation of ST2 cells while MAF1 downregulation inhibited differentiation, indicating MAF1 enhances osteoblast formation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by alkaline phosphatase and alizarin red staining data in Figure 2C-D.

claim: MAF1 downregulation inhibited osteoblast differentiation of ST2 cells.
source: MAF1 overexpression promoted osteoblast differentiation of ST2 cells while MAF1 downregulation inhibited differentiation, indicating MAF1 enhances osteoblast formation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by alkaline phosphatase and alizarin red staining data in Figure 3C-D.

claim: MAF1 enhances osteoblast formation.
source: MAF1 overexpression promoted osteoblast differentiation of ST2 cells while MAF1 downregulation inhibited differentiation, indicating MAF1 enhances osteoblast formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments in ST2 cells.

claim: Other perturbations used to repress RNA pol III transcription inhibited osteoblast differentiation.
source: However, other perturbations used to repress RNA pol III transcription, inhibited osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing ML-60218 treatment (Figure 4) and Brf1 knockdown (Figure 5) decreased osteoblast differentiation.

claim: Decreasing RNA pol III transcription through perturbations other than MAF1 overexpression enhanced adipogenesis in ST2 cells.
source: However, decreasing RNA pol III transcription through these perturbations enhanced adipogenesis in ST2 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Oil red O staining data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The different modalities used to perturb RNA pol III transcription resulted in distinct gene expression changes.
source: The different modalities used to perturb RNA pol III transcription resulted in distinct gene expression changes, indicating that this transcription process is highly sensitive and triggers diverse gene expression programs and phenotypic outcomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: RNA pol III transcription is highly sensitive and triggers diverse gene expression programs and phenotypic outcomes.
source: The different modalities used to perturb RNA pol III transcription resulted in distinct gene expression changes, indicating that this transcription process is highly sensitive and triggers diverse gene expression programs and phenotypic outcomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that different perturbations of RNA pol III transcription produce distinct gene expression profiles.

claim: MAF1 induced genes known to promote osteoblast differentiation.
source: Specifically, MAF1 induced genes known to promote osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq data and GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Genes that are induced during osteoblast differentiation displayed codon bias.
source: Furthermore, genes that are induced during osteoblast differentiation displayed codon bias.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by codon usage analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: MAF1 plays a novel role in osteoblast fate determination, differentiation, and bone mass regulation.
source: Together, these results reveal a novel role for MAF1 and RNA pol III-mediated transcription in osteoblast fate determination, differentiation, and bone mass regulation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: RNA pol III-mediated transcription plays a role in osteoblast fate determination, differentiation, and bone mass regulation.
source: Together, these results reveal a novel role for MAF1 and RNA pol III-mediated transcription in osteoblast fate determination, differentiation, and bone mass regulation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: RNA pol III transcribes various untranslated RNAs including 5S rRNA and tRNAs.
source: RNA polymerase (pol) III transcribes various untranslated RNAs including 5S rRNA and tRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge supported by citations (Dieci et al., 2013; Dieci et al., 2007).

claim: RNA pol III-derived transcripts play essential roles in protein synthesis and secretion.
source: RNA pol III-derived transcripts play essential roles in several processes, including protein synthesis and secretion (Dieci et al., 2013; Dieci et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Transcription of tRNAs requires the recruitment of TFIIIC and TFIIIB to the promoter.
source: In addition to RNA pol III, transcription of tRNAs requires the recruitment of TFIIIC and TFIIIB to the promoter.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: TFIIIB consists of Brf1, TATA-binding protein (TBP) and B-double prime.
source: TFIIIB consists of Brf1, TATA-binding protein (TBP) and B-double prime (Orioli et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: MAF1 binds to RNA pol III and prevents the interaction between RNA pol III and TFIIIB.
source: It binds to RNA pol III and prevents the interaction between RNA pol III and TFIIIB (Vorländer et al., 2019; Vannini et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: MAF1 has been shown to regulate a variety of RNA pol II-transcribed targets.
source: MAF1 has also been shown to regulate a variety of RNA pol II-transcribed targets (Johnson et al., 2007; Palian et al., 2014; Khanna et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2015), and acts as a tumor suppressor (Palian et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016), regulates metabolism (Willis et al., 2018; Bonhoure et al., 2015), and longevity (Shetty et al., 2020; Cai and Wei, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: MAF1 acts as a tumor suppressor.
source: MAF1 has also been shown to regulate a variety of RNA pol II-transcribed targets (Johnson et al., 2007; Palian et al., 2014; Khanna et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2015), and acts as a tumor suppressor (Palian et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016), regulates metabolism (Willis et al., 2018; Bonhoure et al., 2015), and longevity (Shetty et al., 2020; Cai and Wei, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: MAF1 regulates metabolism.
source: MAF1 has also been shown to regulate a variety of RNA pol II-transcribed targets (Johnson et al., 2007; Palian et al., 2014; Khanna et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2015), and acts as a tumor suppressor (Palian et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016), regulates metabolism (Willis et al., 2018; Bonhoure et al., 2015), and longevity (Shetty et al., 2020; Cai and Wei, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: MAF1 regulates longevity.
source: MAF1 has also been shown to regulate a variety of RNA pol II-transcribed targets (Johnson et al., 2007; Palian et al., 2014; Khanna et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2015), and acts as a tumor suppressor (Palian et al., 2014; Li et al., 2016), regulates metabolism (Willis et al., 2018; Bonhoure et al., 2015), and longevity (Shetty et al., 2020; Cai and Wei, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Two RNA pol III isoforms are differentially expressed between pluripotent and differentiated embryonic stem cells (ESCs).
source: Two RNA pol III isoforms are differentially expressed between pluripotent and differentiated embryonic stem cells (ESCs) (Haurie et al., 2010; Wong et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: RNA pol III-dependent transcription modulates the formation of hematopoietic lineages in zebrafish.
source: RNA pol III-dependent transcription also modulates the formation of hematopoietic lineages in zebrafish (Wei et al., 2016) and transcription is downregulated during skeletal muscle differentiation of Xenopus tropicalis (McQueen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: RNA pol III transcription is downregulated during skeletal muscle differentiation of Xenopus tropicalis.
source: RNA pol III-dependent transcription also modulates the formation of hematopoietic lineages in zebrafish (Wei et al., 2016) and transcription is downregulated during skeletal muscle differentiation of Xenopus tropicalis (McQueen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: MAF1 enhances the formation of mesoderm in embryonic stem cells.
source: MAF1 enhances the formation of mesoderm in embryonic stem cells, and the downregulation of RNA pol III-dependent transcription enhances the differentiation of ESCs and 3T3-L1 cells into adipocytes (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: The downregulation of RNA pol III-dependent transcription enhances the differentiation of ESCs and 3T3-L1 cells into adipocytes.
source: MAF1 enhances the formation of mesoderm in embryonic stem cells, and the downregulation of RNA pol III-dependent transcription enhances the differentiation of ESCs and 3T3-L1 cells into adipocytes (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Diseases associated with ribosomal disfunctions, ribosomopathies, are commonly associated with bone marrow, skeletal and craniofacial disorders.
source: Diseases associated with ribosomal disfunctions, ribosomopathies, are commonly associated with bone marrow, skeletal and craniofacial disorders (Trainor and Merrill, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Treacher Collins syndrome is caused by mutations in POLR1C, POLR1D, or TCOF1, which affect rDNA transcription by RNA pol I and ribosome biogenesis.
source: For example, Treacher Collins syndrome is caused by mutations in POLR1C, POLR1D, or TCOF1, which affect rDNA transcription by RNA pol I and ribosome biogenesis (Noack Watt et al., 2016; Dauwerse et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: POLR1C and POLR1D are common subunits of both RNA pol I and RNA pol III.
source: RNA pol III-derived transcripts may also play a role as POLR1C and POLR1D are common subunits of both RNA pol I and RNA pol III.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established scientific knowledge.

claim: In yeast, Treacher Collins syndrome-related mutations in POLR1D result in altered functions of both RNA pol I and III.
source: In yeast, Treacher Collins syndrome-related mutations in POLR1D result in altered functions of both RNA pol I and III (Walker-Kopp et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Cerebellofaciodental syndrome is associated with mutations in the RNA pol III-specific transcription factor, Brf1.
source: Furthermore, RNA pol III-dependent transcription may play a role in cerebellofaciodental syndrome which is associated with mutations in the RNA pol III-specific transcription factor, Brf1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Borck et al., 2015; Jee et al., 2017; Honjo et al., 2021).

claim: Cerebellofaciodental syndrome is characterized by a neurodevelopmental phenotype as well as changes in the facial and dental structure and delayed bone age.
source: This syndrome is characterized by a neurodevelopmental phenotype as well as changes in the facial and dental structure and delayed bone age (Borck et al., 2015; Jee et al., 2017; Honjo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Bone phenotypes have been described in a subgroup of patients with mutations in RNA pol III subunits.
source: Additionally, bone phenotypes have been described in a subgroup of patients with mutations in RNA pol III subunits (Borck et al., 2015; Jee et al., 2017; Honjo et al., 2021; Terhal et al., 2020; Ghoumid et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Osteoblasts and adipocytes are both derived from the mesenchymal lineage.
source: Osteoblasts and adipocytes are both derived from the mesenchymal lineage (Chen et al., 2016) and mutations in BRF1 and RNA pol III subunits are associated with bone-related phenotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Maf1-/- mice showed a significant increase in bone volume, trabecular number, and trabecular thickness in the spine.
source: When compared to age-matched wild-type (WT) mice, Maf1-/- mice showed a significant increase in bone volume, trabecular number, and trabecular thickness in the spine and increased bone volume and trabecular thickness in the tibia.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by µCT data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Maf1-/- mice showed increased bone volume and trabecular thickness in the tibia.
source: When compared to age-matched wild-type (WT) mice, Maf1-/- mice showed a significant increase in bone volume, trabecular number, and trabecular thickness in the spine and increased bone volume and trabecular thickness in the tibia.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by µCT data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Bone formation parameters, mineralizing surface, mineral apposition rate, and bone formation rate, were significantly increased in the spine of Maf1-/- mice.
source: This showed that bone formation parameters, mineralizing surface, mineral apposition rate, and bone formation rate, were significantly increased in the spine.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Tibiae of Maf1-/- mice showed an increase in mineralization surface.
source: Tibiae showed an increase in mineralization surface.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The increase in bone mass in Maf1-/- mice is due to increased bone formation.
source: Overall, these data suggest that the increase in bone mass in Maf1-/- mice is due to increased bone formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the histomorphometric data showing increased bone formation parameters.

claim: Osteoclastogenesis was increased in cells derived from Maf1-/- mice.
source: Surprisingly, osteoblast formation was reduced, while osteoclastogenesis was increased in cells derived from Maf1-/- mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by TRAP staining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: MAF1 increases osteoblast formation in long-term ex vivo cultures.
source: This suggests that MAF1 increases osteoblast and decreases osteoclast formation in long-term ex vivo cultures.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ex vivo culture data from Maf1-/- mice.

claim: MAF1 decreases osteoclast formation in long-term ex vivo cultures.
source: This suggests that MAF1 increases osteoblast and decreases osteoclast formation in long-term ex vivo cultures.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ex vivo culture data from Maf1-/- mice.

claim: The increase in bone formation in Maf1-/- mice is likely the result of non-cell-autonomous effects arising from the deletion of MAF1 in other tissues.
source: Because ex vivo cultures are not affected by signals originating from external tissues, we hypothesized that the increase in bone formation in Maf1-/- mice is likely the result of non-cell-autonomous effects arising from the deletion of MAF1 in other tissues.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the discrepancy between in vivo and ex vivo phenotypes.

claim: MAF1 overexpression in osteoblasts would be expected to increase osteoblastogenesis.
source: The ex vivo data indicate that MAF1 is a positive regulator of osteoblast differentiation, and its overexpression in osteoblasts would therefore be expected to increase osteoblastogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ex vivo data showing reduced osteoblastogenesis in Maf1-/- cells.

claim: Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice showed a ~16 fold increase in MAF1 transgene expression compared to endogenous MAF1 mRNA.
source: qRT-PCR showed a ~16 fold increase in MAF1 transgene expression compared to endogenous MAF1 mRNA (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: No gross phenotypic changes were observed in Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice.
source: No gross phenotypic changes were observed, and the weight of the mice at 12 weeks was unchanged (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by weight data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The weight of Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice at 12 weeks was unchanged compared to controls.
source: No gross phenotypic changes were observed, and the weight of the mice at 12 weeks was unchanged (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by weight data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: MAF1 overexpression in Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice led to an increase in bone volume, trabecular number and thickness, and connectivity density.
source: MAF1 overexpression in Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice led to an increase in bone volume, trabecular number and thickness, and connectivity density, and a corresponding reduction in trabecular separation when compared with Cre-controls.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by µCT data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: MAF1 overexpression in Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice led to a reduction in trabecular separation.
source: MAF1 overexpression in Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice led to an increase in bone volume, trabecular number and thickness, and connectivity density, and a corresponding reduction in trabecular separation when compared with Cre-controls.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by µCT data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cortical thickness was not significantly increased in Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice.
source: Cortical thickness was not significantly increased (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by µCT data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Histomorphometric analysis of Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice confirmed an increase in trabecular number and a reduction in trabecular separation.
source: Histomorphometric analysis confirmed an increase in trabecular number and a reduction in trabecular separation, while other parameters were not significantly affected (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by histomorphometric data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Primary stromal cells from Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice displayed an increase in MAF1 expression.
source: These primary cells displayed an increase in MAF1 expression and showed a corresponding decrease in tRNA gene transcription (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Primary stromal cells from Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice showed a decrease in tRNA gene transcription.
source: These primary cells displayed an increase in MAF1 expression and showed a corresponding decrease in tRNA gene transcription (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: MAF1-overexpressing stromal cells showed an increase in their mineralizing capacity.
source: When MAF1-overexpressing stromal cells were allowed to differentiate into bone-forming osteoblasts in media containing ascorbic acid and β-glycerolphosphate, there was a clear increase in their mineralizing capacity seen by alizarin red staining (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by alizarin red staining data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: MAF1 enhances the differentiation or function of osteoblasts.
source: These results suggest that MAF1 enhances the differentiation or function of osteoblasts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the increased mineralization observed in MAF1-overexpressing cells.

claim: There was no change in the osteoclastogenic cytokines RANKL and OPG in the femurs of Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice.
source: We found no change in the osteoclastogenic cytokines receptor activator of NF-κβ ligand (RANKL) and osteoprotegerin (OPG) in the femurs, indicating that changes in the OPG/RANKL ratio did not play a role (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Changes in the OPG/RANKL ratio did not play a role in the bone phenotype of Prx1-Cre; LSL-MAF1 mice.
source: We found no change in the osteoclastogenic cytokines receptor activator of NF-κβ ligand (RANKL) and osteoprotegerin (OPG) in the femurs, indicating that changes in the OPG/RANKL ratio did not play a role (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of change in RANKL and OPG expression.

claim: Ectopic MAF1 expression resulted in the reduction of pre-tRNAIle and pre-tRNALeu gene transcription in ST2 cells.
source: Ectopic MAF1 expression was confirmed by western blot (Figure 2A) and qRT-PCR and resulted in the reduction of pre-tRNAIle and pre-tRNALeu gene transcription (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: MAF1 overexpression resulted in enhanced staining for alkaline phosphatase (Alp) in ST2 cells.
source: MAF1 overexpression resulted in enhanced staining for alkaline phosphatase (Alp), a marker for early osteoblast differentiation (Figure 2C), as well as increased in vitro mineralization as noted on alizarin red staining (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by alkaline phosphatase staining shown in Figure 2C.

claim: MAF1 overexpression resulted in increased in vitro mineralization in ST2 cells.
source: MAF1 overexpression resulted in enhanced staining for alkaline phosphatase (Alp), a marker for early osteoblast differentiation (Figure 2C), as well as increased in vitro mineralization as noted on alizarin red staining (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by alizarin red staining shown in Figure 2D.

claim: MAF1 overexpression resulted in a significant increase in the expression of osteoblast marker genes Col1A, Sp7, osteocalcin, Alp, and Bsp in ST2 cells.
source: MAF1 overexpression also resulted in a significant increase in the expression of osteoblast marker genes, namely collagen type 1 alpha (Col1A), Sp7, osteocalcin, Alp, and bone sialoprotein (Bsp) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: MAF1 knockdown resulted in an increase in pre-tRNA expression in ST2 cells.
source: As expected, this resulted in an increase in pre-tRNA expression, particularly on day 10 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: MAF1 knockdown resulted in a decrease in Alp staining in ST2 cells.
source: MAF1 knockdown resulted in a decrease in Alp staining (Figure 3C) and a robust reduction in mineralization (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by alkaline phosphatase staining shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MAF1 knockdown resulted in a robust reduction in mineralization in ST2 cells.
source: MAF1 knockdown resulted in a decrease in Alp staining (Figure 3C) and a robust reduction in mineralization (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by alizarin red staining shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Osteoblast markers Sp7, Alp, and Bsp were significantly downregulated in MAF1 knockdown ST2 cells.
source: Osteoblast markers, namely Sp7, Alp, and Bsp were significantly downregulated in these cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: MAF1 functions to promote osteoblast differentiation.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that MAF1 functions to promote osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments in ST2 cells.

claim: Reduced expression of MAF1 in ST2 cells resulted in a decrease in osteoblast differentiation.
source: Reduced expression of MAF1 in ST2 cells and in bone marrow stromal cells derived from Maf1-/- mice resulted in a decrease in osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Reduced expression of MAF1 in bone marrow stromal cells derived from Maf1-/- mice resulted in a decrease in osteoblast differentiation.
source: Reduced expression of MAF1 in ST2 cells and in bone marrow stromal cells derived from Maf1-/- mice resulted in a decrease in osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: MAF1 overexpression in ST2 cells increased osteoblast differentiation.
source: MAF1 overexpression in ST2 cells increased osteoblast differentiation while MAF1 overexpression, specifically in the mesenchymal cells of the long bones, increased bone mass.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: MAF1 overexpression, specifically in the mesenchymal cells of the long bones, increased bone mass.
source: MAF1 overexpression in ST2 cells increased osteoblast differentiation while MAF1 overexpression, specifically in the mesenchymal cells of the long bones, increased bone mass.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1D.

claim: The paradoxical phenotype in Maf1-/- mice likely resulted from yet uncharacterized, non-cell-autonomous confounding effects on osteoblasts arising from global MAF1 deletion.
source: The paradoxical phenotype in Maf1-/- mice therefore likely resulted from yet uncharacterized, non-cell-autonomous confounding effects on osteoblasts arising from global MAF1 deletion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the contrasting phenotypes observed in global knockout versus tissue-specific overexpression.

claim: MAF1 has been shown to promote adipogenesis since knockdown of MAF1 in pre-adipocytes reduces adipocyte formation.
source: Finally, MAF1 has been shown to promote adipogenesis since knockdown of MAF1 in pre-adipocytes reduces adipocyte formation (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation.

claim: MAF1 overexpression produced an increase in Oil red O stained cells in ST2 cells.
source: We found that MAF1 overexpression produced an increase in Oil red O stained cells and upregulated the expression of adipogenesis genes Pparg, Cebpa and Fabp4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Oil red O staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: MAF1 overexpression upregulated the expression of adipogenesis genes Pparg, Cebpa and Fabp4 in ST2 cells.
source: We found that MAF1 overexpression produced an increase in Oil red O stained cells and upregulated the expression of adipogenesis genes Pparg, Cebpa and Fabp4 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Primary cells from Maf1-/- mice showed increased tRNA transcription.
source: These cells showed increased tRNA transcription as expected and showed decreased differentiation into adipocytes as seen by Oil Red O stain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Primary cells from Maf1-/- mice showed decreased differentiation into adipocytes.
source: These cells showed increased tRNA transcription as expected and showed decreased differentiation into adipocytes as seen by Oil Red O stain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Oil Red O staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Histological analysis of femurs from 12-week-old Maf1-/- mice showed that both adipocyte number and adipocyte volume was reduced.
source: Consistent with these results, histological analysis of femurs from 12-week-old Maf1-/- mice showed that both adipocyte number and adipocyte volume was reduced (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by histological data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In addition to promoting osteogenesis, MAF1 enhances adipocyte differentiation.
source: These results confirm that in addition to promoting osteogenesis, MAF1 enhances adipocyte differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the adipocyte differentiation experiments.

claim: tRNA gene transcription was significantly reduced by ML-60218 treatment in ST2 cells.
source: tRNA gene transcription was significantly reduced by ML-60218 treatment (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Reduction of RNA pol III transcription by ML-60218 resulted in a decrease in Alp and Alizarin red staining in ST2 cells.
source: However, in contrast to what was observed with MAF1 overexpression, reduction of RNA pol III transcription by ML-60218 resulted in a decrease in Alp and Alizarin red staining (Figure 4B and C) and a significant reduction in the expression of osteoblast marker genes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by staining data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Reduction of RNA pol III transcription by ML-60218 resulted in a significant reduction in the expression of osteoblast marker genes in ST2 cells.
source: However, in contrast to what was observed with MAF1 overexpression, reduction of RNA pol III transcription by ML-60218 resulted in a decrease in Alp and Alizarin red staining (Figure 4B and C) and a significant reduction in the expression of osteoblast marker genes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The differentiation of primary stromal cells derived from C57BL/6 mice was significantly reduced by ML-60218 treatment.
source: This effect was not specific to ST2 cells, as the differentiation of primary stromal cells derived from C57BL/6 mice was also significantly reduced by ML-60218 treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Brf1 knockdown decreased Alp and Alizarin red staining in ST2 cells.
source: Similar to ML-60218 treatment, Brf1 knockdown decreased Alp and Alizarin red staining, as well as osteoblast marker expression (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by staining data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Brf1 knockdown decreased osteoblast marker expression in ST2 cells.
source: Similar to ML-60218 treatment, Brf1 knockdown decreased Alp and Alizarin red staining, as well as osteoblast marker expression (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: While different approaches to decrease RNA pol III-dependent transcription all affect osteoblast differentiation, increased MAF1 expression promotes differentiation, while Brf1 knockdown and ML-60218 treatment repress osteoblast differentiation.
source: These results indicate that, while different approaches to decrease RNA pol III-dependent transcription all affect osteoblast differentiation, increased MAF1 expression promotes differentiation, while Brf1 knockdown and ML-60218 treatment repress osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the comparison of different approaches to manipulate RNA pol III transcription.
